clue.text: GA's neighbour with limitless vote for old tax

parts.note: GA is Georgia; South Carolina, abbreviated SC, borders it

indicators.note: without limits means the word vote loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A US electoral grumble: a nearby state's vote somehow tied to an old levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limitless' strips the ends from VOTE, leaving OT. The old tax survives in the phrase 'scot-free'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scot was a historical levy or assessment paid in medieval England and Scotland.

clue.text: Some voting early, having shifted from neutral

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some early voters have already moved off the fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A car taken out of neutral has a gear engaged, ready to move.

clue.text: Lots of data about slight Southern squalor

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: files hold lots of data
slight means thin

explanation.surface: A dossier of evidence about slight squalor in the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalor is a state of dirt and neglect, the same as foulness or grime.

clue.text: Turn up old form of address for Georgia writer

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the word from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: sirrah is an archaic, contemptuous way of addressing a man

explanation.surface: A Georgia author shows up wearing an outdated title.
explanation.walkthrough: Joel Chandler Harris, author of the Uncle Remus stories, was from Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Joel Chandler Harris was a Georgian author famed for the Uncle Remus folk tales.

clue.text: Guided the wrong way, knowing state of successful 9

indicators.note: the wrong way means the word for guided is read backwards

parts.note: guided means led
knowing means aware

explanation.surface: A shrewd guide leads the winning candidate's home state the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: The successful candidate (9 across) was Joe Biden, long a senator from this state.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Biden, the winning presidential candidate, represented this small East Coast state in the Senate.

clue.text: Called, sought election? Good

parts.note: to run is to stand for election

explanation.surface: A candidate phoned round: did they seek election? Good.
explanation.definitionFit: Rang is the past tense of ring, meaning telephoned someone.

clue.text: Dessert from flipping United States — I ruin it

indicators.note: flipping means the whole string of pieces is turned back to front

parts.note: to mar is to ruin
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook blames a dessert disaster on a turbulent America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild expletive but reverses USIMARIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian layered pudding of coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone.

clue.text: Supporting Democrat as president

parts.note: to be for something is to support it

explanation.surface: Backing a Democrat for the White House.
explanation.walkthrough: Gerald Ford was in fact a Republican, which the surface plays against.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Ford was the 38th US president, succeeding Nixon in 1974.

clue.text: Would-be president, say, apt to speak frankly, scoffed

parts.note: someone candid is apt to speak frankly
to scoff food is to eat it greedily, so ate

explanation.surface: A blunt-talking presidential hopeful was mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffed' suggests jeering, but here means gobbled food.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone running for an office, the presidency for example, is a contender for it.

clue.text: I run after a male pal

indicators.note: after says the pieces I and run come behind a male

parts.note: to go is to run, as a machine does

explanation.surface: I jog behind a male friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, used informally in English for a buddy.

clue.text: Communicate what means little, time after time

indicators.note: after places the second time at the end, behind the word for little

parts.note: wee is a Scottish word meaning little

explanation.surface: A dictionary note: one word for little, repeated over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: To post a short message on social media, as Trump famously did, is to put a thought across online.

clue.text: Diehards bring up a drug, oddly

parts.note: to rear a child is to bring it up

indicators.note: oddly means the letters of a drug are arranged in an odd, unusual way

explanation.surface: Hardliners raise a narcotic in strange fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' tempts a pick of alternate letters, but A, R, G is useless; it is an anagram of A DRUG.
explanation.definitionFit: The rearguard of a party is its conservative faction, resisting change to the last.

clue.text: Lots of politicians do OK on links and connexions

parts.note: on a golf course (links), a respectable score for a hole is par
ties are connections; connexion is an old British spelling

explanation.surface: Politicians play passable golf and network.
explanation.definitionFit: Political groupings such as Democrats or Republicans are organised bodies of politicians.

clue.text: Bird — it is south of where some in flock gather

indicators.note: in a down clue, being south of something means coming below it, so after it

parts.note: a pew is a church bench where a congregation, a priest's flock, sits

explanation.surface: A bird nests below the gathering point of a flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flock' suggests birds, but means a church congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: The lapwing, a plover of fields and moors, is named for its call.

clue.text: A part of Trump's issue in one state, or all of them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: MA is the abbreviation for Massachusetts
Eric is one of Donald Trump's children, his issue

explanation.surface: One of Trump's sons is an issue in one state, or across the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means offspring, not a political question.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is the union of all fifty states taken together.

clue.text: Axe the liar, needing change — cheer up, bigly

indicators.note: needing change says these letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fire the liar and things must change; that will cheer people up, bigly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bigly' is a word associated with Trump, making the definition mean cheer up hugely.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrill or elate someone is to lift their spirits greatly.

clue.text: States opposed omitting conclusion

indicators.note: omitting conclusion means the last letter of the word for opposed is dropped

parts.note: averse means opposed

explanation.surface: States hostile to something leave out the ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like US states but is a verb, meaning declares.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to declare firmly, so it matches asserting something as true.

clue.text: First to go on board with partners securing success

indicators.note: securing means the partners hold the next piece between them

parts.note: in bridge, West and East (W and E) play as partners
a hit is a success

explanation.surface: A newcomer on the board, flanked by allies, scores a win.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess the player with the pale pieces always moves first.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the pale side opens the game, so it is the first to move on the board.

clue.text: Repeatedly runs bad treaties

indicators.note: bad means the letters of treaties are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Poor agreements keep being rerun.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to perform a process again and again, as in a computer loop.

clue.text: Ordinary man's book abridged

indicators.note: abridged means the word for book is shortened by its final letter

parts.note: Joel is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: An everyman's book, cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to Joe Biden, cast as an everyman.
explanation.definitionFit: An average Joe is a typical, unremarkable guy.

clue.text: Judge joining outside court as meeting place

indicators.note: outside means the word for joining goes round the court

parts.note: a union is a joining

explanation.surface: A judge links an outside court to a venue for meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads or railway lines meet at one, so it is where they come together.

clue.text: Legislative assembly, in practice, following call to attend

indicators.note: following means the practice piece comes after the call

parts.note: ho is an exclamation to attract attention
use is practice or custom

explanation.surface: A legislature, in practice, convenes after a summons.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Representatives is one chamber of the US Congress.

clue.text: Serious disloyalty from maverick senator

indicators.note: maverick means unorthodox, so the letters of senator go their own way

explanation.surface: Betrayal by a rebellious senator.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's own country is the gravest form of disloyalty.

clue.text: Votes completely screened by machines

indicators.note: screened by means the first piece is hidden inside the second

parts.note: bots are automated machines or programs
all means completely

explanation.surface: Votes entirely vetted by machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballots are the papers or acts by which electors cast their choices.

clue.text: Ordered new leader with extra heart?

indicators.note: with extra means an additional letter is inserted

parts.note: Joe Biden was the newly elected US leader
the heart of the leader's name is its middle letter, D, here added again

explanation.surface: Was the new president bossy, or just extra-hearted?
explanation.definitionFit: Bidden is a past participle of bid, meaning commanded or told to do something.

clue.text: Drop a question that, in part, is not clear

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a portion of these words

explanation.surface: Abandon a question that is partly unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something murky or impenetrable cannot be seen through, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Grouped together in plot around illegal scheme

indicators.note: around means the plot surrounds the scheme

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
a racket is a dishonest scheme

explanation.surface: Conspirators lumped together in a plot round a crooked scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Items set in brackets are joined as a unit, as are ranked equals.

clue.text: President in wilderness

definitions.meaning: either George ..., father or son, US presidents

explanation.definitionFit: Two Bushes held the US presidency, and the bush is untamed backcountry.

clue.text: A 19 down in Kentucky for Coolidge's girl

indicators.note: in means these pieces sit inside the state

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to 19 down is a meeting of roads, and a T is a type of one

explanation.surface: A road junction in Kentucky named for President Coolidge's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coolidge' suggests President Calvin Coolidge, but it is Susan Coolidge, author of the novel What Katy Did.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan Coolidge wrote What Katy Did, whose heroine is the girl named here.

clue.text: Answer about a NE state

parts.note: re means about or concerning
CT is the abbreviation for Connecticut, in the north-east US

explanation.surface: A reply concerning a north-eastern state.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond to something is to answer it with action or words.

clue.text: Character flaw seen in party politics

indicators.note: seen in says the answer is visible inside these words

explanation.surface: A personal failing on display in partisan politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character flaw' reads as a moral weakness, but means an error in a printed character.
explanation.definitionFit: A misprinted letter in text is a fault in one typed symbol.

clue.text: Pence in Wild West got the brush?

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
wild means the letters of west are scattered

explanation.surface: Vice President Pence out in the Wild West got the brush-off?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges WEST into SWET, and 'in' puts P inside it. 'Pence' suggests Mike Pence but is just pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: Using a broom or brush on a floor is to clean it in long strokes.

clue.text: Public behind attempt to win playing trick

parts.note: overt means open or public
the rump is the behind

explanation.surface: A public backside makes a bid to win: a dig at Trump.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games, playing a higher trump than one already played on a trick tries to take it.
